results.notes: Rule 5 set-diversity result, in raw numbers of submissions containing the keyword. As in the extraction, treatment_mean and control_mean store whole-pool counts, NOT participant-level means; difference is the treatment pool count minus the control pool count, not a difference in rates. Participant SDs, a randomization-level SE, and se_type are null because this extracted outcome is one total per set. No binary-rate outcome was substituted and no HC2, paired, or cluster SE is claimed. Printed totals checked against main PDF p. 1 (printed p. 1107); people counts checked against supplement PDF pp. 3-4, Table 1. Use exp_2a/Exp2A.main.full.csv, one unique workerId and ResponseId per person, selecting Condition=Chatbot versus Condition=None. Retain every supplied analyzed person. The original Exp2A Rmd was read as text only. Independently applying its valid-ID, completion/demographics, attention-check, and six explicit nonsensical-response exclusions to the raw Qualtrics CSV gives 414, 298, 297, 291 rows respectively; the final 291 identities, conditions and idea texts match the posted full dataset exactly. Human-only Condition is the literal string None, not missing. The headerless pool CSVs match these participant texts, with one ChatGPT apostrophe encoding artifact normalized only for linking. Keyword counts are computed on unmodified pool texts and independently checked on original participant texts. Case-insensitive substring matching recovers 20/96 ChatGPT, 7/100 web-search and 12/95 human-only. A case-sensitive substring would give 19 for ChatGPT; a singular-only whole-word search would give 11 for human-only. Including the plural and ignoring case recovers all three published totals. All input hashes match the download manifest. Between-person assignment; there is no within-person or first-round contrast.
